title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: BitRiver founder charged in Russia over alleged $8M fraud
summary: Russian authorities charged BitRiver founder Igor Runets with alleged fraud tied to a $8 million crypto mining equipment deal involving Russian billionaire Oleg Deripaska.

title: Samsung unit explores stablecoin infrastructure with Upbit’s operator
summary: Samsung SDS is discussing stablecoin infrastructure and AI-based payment models with Dunamu, the operator of South Korean crypto exchange Upbit.

title: Hedge fund with $1.1B in Bitcoin miner stocks seeks capital after AI sell-off: FT
summary: The FT said Situational Awareness has approached investors and lenders after borrowing amplified losses during July’s AI stock sell-off.

title: Australia sues Telegram over alleged failures to remove terror content
summary: Telegram faces Australian court proceedings after eSafety alleged the platform failed to detect and remove extremist material shared by users.

title: Chinese newspaper warns of Bitcoin extortion scam using its name
summary: China Business Journal says fraudsters impersonated the publication, demanding Bitcoin to suppress purported investigative reports about targeted companies.

title: Bitcoin ETF inflows return as Ether funds slip into outflows
summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $32.1 million in inflows on Wednesday despite Bitcoin dipping below $64,000, ending a four-session outflow streak.

title: South Korea report proposes stablecoin rules before crypto law
summary: Policy report recommends interim licensing guidance, greater flexibility for stablecoin issuers and rules ahead of the Digital Asset Basic Act.

title: US sanctions Iranian maritime firm, says it accepted Bitcoin to evade restrictions
summary: The US Treasury said HormuzSafe accepted Bitcoin and other digital assets to evade sanctions and generate revenue for Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

title: Luno cuts 20% of staff as crypto layoffs spread across 12 firms in July
summary: Luno and Gnosis joined a widening round of crypto restructurings in July, when at least 12 companies reported job cuts.
